title: Intra-Omental Islet Transplantation Using h-Omental Matrix Islet filliNG (hOMING)
protocol: Chemically induce diabetes in recipient rats.
Inject 75 mg/kg of streptozotocin intraperitoneally to rats.
Check the diabetes status by daily blood glucose measurements during the first four days.
Inject long-acting insulin 6 U/day subcutaneously when rats exhibit glycemia over 2 g/L.
Include rats in the cohort when two measures of tail vein blood glucose are >4-5 g/L for 2 consecutive days, and C-peptide level is <200 pM.
Measure glycemia using a glucometer.
Measure C-peptidemia by an enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).
Implant insulin pellets under the skin.
Anesthetize the rat using gas anesthesia (3% isoflurane in 500 mL/min O2).
Place the anesthetized rat in the prone position.
Verify the absence of reflex response by paw pinching to confirm anesthesia status.
Clean the neck area with povidone iodine.
Shave the cleaned area using a razor blade.
Apply povidone iodine again and let it stand for 3 min.
Sterilize 1.5 insulin pellets in a 1:5 diluted povidone iodine solution.
Pierce the neck skin using a 16 G trocar.
Insert the sterilized pellet using the furnished guide and stylet.
Retrieve the guide and stylet after insertion.
Stitch one point at the insertion site.
Clean the stitch with povidone iodine.
Allow the rat to recover from anesthesia.
Ensure rats have access to food to avoid hypoglycemia.
Measure glycaemia decrease after implantation to evaluate pellet efficiency.
Monitor glycemia level every week for 1 month post-implantation.
Include rats in the cohort when tail vein blood C-peptide level is maintained under 200 pM one month after insulin pellet implantation.
Reconstitute alginate powder in sterile PBS at a concentration of 1.5%.
Sterilize the alginate solution by passage through a 0.22 µm filter.
Prepare 400 µL of islet carrier per recipient.
Isolate islets from healthy Lewis rats (200-250 g).
Count islets in islet equivalents (IEQ), with one IEQ equivalent to a pancreatic islet with a diameter of 150 µm.
Wash islet aliquots with 500 µL of CMRL medium free of fetal bovine serum.
Pellet the islets by centrifugation at 500 x g for 2 minutes at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant after centrifuging.
Add 150 µL of alginate hydrogel carrier over the islets and mix carefully.
Place the mixed solution on ice.
Prepare an atraumatic 21 G needle and load it with 150 µL of empty alginate into a 1 mL syringe without dead volume.
Fill the syringe with the mixture of islets and alginate (total volume 300 µL).
Keep the filled syringe on ice.
Shave the neck area using a razor blade.
Sterilize the shaved area with povidone iodine.
Let the iodine stand for 3 min.
Make an incision using a scalpel.
Remove the 1.5 insulin pellets using forceps.
Close the skin using one or two single stitch points.
Shave and sterilize the peritoneal area with povidone iodine.
Let the iodine stand for 3 min.
Create a 1.5 cm laparotomy just under the sternum using a scalpel.
Place wet-sterile gauze around the incised area.
Identify the omentum, which is the fat pad localized next to the stomach.
Use forceps to carefully catch the omentum and pull it gently out of the peritoneal cavity.
Spread the omentum on the gauze.
Hydrate the omental tissue well using 2 mL of pre-warmed 37 °C sterile saline.
Manipulate the tissue with small curved forceps.
Penetrate the omental edge with a needle between the omental layers.
Insert the needle entirely into the tissue.
Start the injection of the islet preparation slowly.
Carefully move the needle backward to inject the islets in several places (as lines).
Ensure that the hydrogel has stopped exiting the needle before withdrawing it.
Repeat this manipulation as needed to inject the entire contents of the syringe using different entry points.
Check that islets are not clustered in the syringe at the end of the injections.
Withdraw the needle from the syringe if some islets remain visible.
Fill the syringe directly with 100 μL of empty hydrogel and reconnect the needle.
Perform a second round of injection to flush out remaining islets.
Hydrate the omental tissue and the wall of the laparotomy using sterile saline.
Replace the omentum in the abdominal cavity carefully using forceps.
Inject 2 mL of pre-warmed sterile saline into the abdominal cavity to rehydrate the rat.
Close the muscle wall using a continuous thread suture.
Stitch the cutaneous layer with single stitch point (point-by-point).
Inject meloxicam (1.5 mg/kg) subcutaneously as an analgesic for  five days once a day.
Place the rat in a cage on a heating pad until recovery from anesthesia.
Measure blood glucose after transplantation every day.
If glycemia is >2 g/L, inject 6 U of long-acting insulin subcutaneously once a day.
Assess graft function by monitoring glycemia and c-peptidemia over 1 or 2 months.
Anesthetize the rat with gas anesthesia and place it in the supine position.
Shave the peritoneal area and sterilize it using povidone iodine for 3 min.
Create a 1.5 cm laparotomy just under sternum using a scalpel.
Place wet-sterile gauze all around the incised area.
Identify the omentum, which is next to the stomach.
Use forceps to carefully spread it on the gauze.
Use scissors to excise the omentum starting from the part that adheres onto the pancreas tail (next to the spleen).
If bleeding occurs, use dry sterile gauze to stop it.
Continue excision along the part attached to the stomach and retrieve the omentum.
Check if any bleeding persists.
If no bleeding persists, inject 2 mL of pre-warmed saline.
Close the rat and process as previously described.
Inject insulin (6 U/SC/day) into explanted animals to maintain well-being.
Euthanize the rat with an overdose of pentobarbital (182.2 mg/kg) 10 to 12 days after explantation.
Fix retrieved omenta using 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA).
Embed fixed omenta in paraffin.
Cut sections 4 µm in thickness.
Apply hematoxylin and eosin stain for morphological evaluation of the transplant.
Determine statistical significance using statistical analysis software.
Perform repeated measures analysis of variance (ANOVA).
Use Tukey’s honest significance difference test as a post hoc test.
Represent p values as: *p < 0.05; ** p < 0.01; *** p < 0.001.
